newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Blue chips, Wall Street drag down Singapore shares.
newsitem.headline: Blue chips, Wall Street drag down Singapore shares.

text.p: Singapore shares lost momentum on Monday and closed down on a combination of domestic blue chip sell-offs and concerns about the heavy drop on Wall Street.
"We've pretty well been running on the spot today," said one dealer as the Straits Times Industrials Index closed down 34.95 points at 1,918.85, retracing much of Friday's 62-point gain.
The STII's close was a 27-point rebound from its intra-day low of 1,891.05.
Dealers said downward pressure came from a handful of blue chips with foreign and domestic share tranches at the centre of speculation about the future of dual listings.
Domestic tranches can only be bought by Singaporeans. Foreign tranches are open to all buyers.

Statements last week from the Stock Exchange of Singapore, the Monetary Authority of Singapore and some of the companies involved helped assuage fears of the system's abandonment, prompting a bounce-back in foreign tranches on Monday.
"Most of our fall today is to do with local issues rather than Wall Street," said a dealer at a local institution.
Singapore Press Holdings foreign headed gainers, up a dollar at Singapore $23.00. DBS Bank foreign jumped S$0.90 to S$16.70 and UOB foreign regained S$0.80 to end at S$13.10.
But DBS local shares, dropped S$0.65 to S$9.75, SPH domestic shares fell 40 cents to S$14.50 and the local issue of Singapore Airlines was down S$0.35 to S$8.10.
SIA foreign shares gained 40 cents to S$11.40 and were active with 3.4 million shares changing hands, although almost two thirds of them crossed in off-market deals.
Dealers said many of the total of 207 million shares traded on Monday were crossed rather than traded on the open market, showing signs of some mopping up of oversold positions.
Bearish sentiment was clear though with losers swamping gainers 369 to 42.
